text.arabic_uthmani: لِّكُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكًا هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ ۖ فَلَا يُنَٰزِعُنَّكَ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ ۚ وَٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ۖ إِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ

words.gloss_range: initial preposition of allocation, benefit, and purpose governing the universal phrase
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) opens the ayah by making allocation the first grammatical move. It governs {{ar:كُلِّ}} ({{tr:kulli}}), and the phrase reaches {{ar:أُمَّةٍ}} ({{tr:ummatin}}) before the verb appears, so the reader receives the universal recipient-scope before the divine appointment is named.

topics.headline: allocation opens before the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins with allocated scope, not with a bare act of making.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the genitive quantifier phrase and stands before the perfect verb, so allocation and fronting are locally forced.

words.gloss_range: distributive totality: each community individually within a fronted allocation phrase
words.root_gloss_range: totality, completeness, and encircling coverage; local construct grammar selects distributive eachness
words.prose: {{ar:كُلِّ}} ({{tr:kulli}}) is the construct head inside the opening allocation phrase. Its singular form distributes over {{ar:أُمَّةٍ}} ({{tr:ummatin}}), so the clause is not about one mass community but about each community receiving its appointed rite. The fronted phrase also makes universality the topic before {{ar:جَعَلْنَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnā}}) arrives, and that formula recalls the rite wording at 22:34.

topics.headline: construct totality distributes each community
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that universality is counted community by community rather than stated as a vague collective total.
topics.reason: The construct with an indefinite second term supports distributive eachness; broader totality imagery is retained only as coverage pressure.

topics.headline: universal phrase precedes divine agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the discourse sets the universal communal frame before naming the act of appointment.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is placed before the verb and marks the shift into communal legal discourse.

topics.headline: rite formula reprises 22:34
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the opening as part of the 22:34 every-community rite formula rather than as an isolated statement.
topics.reason: The rows link the quantifier to community, appointment, and the concrete 22:34 formula.

words.gloss_range: indefinite collective community as the second term of the distributive construct
words.root_gloss_range: community, direction, leadership, and sourcehood; local plural performers select community over period or exemplar senses
words.prose: {{ar:أُمَّةٍ}} ({{tr:ummatin}}) keeps the recipient class open: no named group is singled out. Under {{ar:كُلِّ}} ({{tr:kulli}}), each instance of community is treated as a collective unit, then the later {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) expands that unit into actual plural performers. Its root field adds orientation and source imagery, while the local performers block readings such as a time-span or lone exemplar. The wording also reactivates the ritual-community frame at 22:34.

topics.headline: indefinite community under each
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim applies to every kind of community without naming or limiting the list.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite genitive as the second construct term under the distributive quantifier.

topics.headline: community selected from a broader root field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices community as an oriented collective, not merely an ethnic count or abstract category.
topics.reason: The root family supports direction, leadership, and sourcehood; local plural performers select the collective-community branch.

topics.headline: community and rite echo 22:34
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the beginning of the ayah as a return to the 22:34 community-and-rite frame, now moving toward invitation.
topics.reason: The rows give a concrete 22:34 parallel and connect the opening collective field to the closing uprightness field.

words.gloss_range: perfect first-person plural appointing or rendering a rite within a universal distribution frame
words.root_gloss_range: making, placing, rendering, appointing; local object frame selects functional appointment rather than creation from nothing
words.prose: {{ar:جَعَلْنَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnā}}) arrives after the recipient phrase, so the verb confirms an already established universal scope. Its perfect first-person plural form presents the rite as an already completed divine appointment. The root can cover making and placing, but with {{ar:مَنسَكًا}} ({{tr:mansakan}}) as the object it narrows to functional appointment or rendering, not creation from nothing, and it repeats the appointment formula of 22:34.

topics.headline: completed divine appointment, not creation from nothing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rite is established by divine agency as an appointed function, not negotiated into being by communities.
topics.reason: The perfect 1cp morphology binds the subject to the completed act, while the object frame selects appointment from the broader making range.

topics.headline: appointed object receives performer clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb governs more than an object: the rite is immediately qualified by those who perform it.
topics.reason: The local syntax gives the verb an object and then a nominal clause describing that object through performance.

topics.headline: appointment verb reprises 22:34
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the 22:34 appointment wording returning as a structural marker for the rite section.
topics.reason: The rows tie this verb to the same-surah 22:34 formula and to the local community, ritual, and lordship roots.

words.gloss_range: appointed ritual unit: rite, act, place, time, and sacrificial practice held together by an indefinite mafʿal form
words.root_gloss_range: devotion, sacrifice, ritual performance, and purification; local object position selects the appointed rite while preserving concrete ritual undertones
words.prose: {{ar:مَنسَكًا}} ({{tr:mansakan}}) is the appointed object of {{ar:جَعَلْنَا}} ({{tr:jaʿalnā}}). Its indefinite mafʿal shape leaves the ritual unit open as practice, place, occasion, or rite, while the root field keeps sacrifice, devotion, and purification close to the surface. The same root then returns in {{ar:نَاسِكُوهُ}} ({{tr:nāsikūhu}}), so the appointed practice and the performers of it are tied together, and the word recalls the ritual appointment at 22:34.

topics.headline: rite object with act-place-time breadth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the appointed object is a technical ritual unit, not a generic worship word or flat object.
topics.reason: The noun-of-time/place form and indefinite accusative preserve act, locus, and occasion breadth, while object syntax selects the appointed rite.

topics.headline: same root links rite and performers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rite and its performers are built from the same root, making performance part of the appointed object’s identity.
topics.reason: The rows point to the immediate root reprise from the appointed ritual noun to the active-participle performer form.

words.gloss_range: independent third-person plural pronoun opening the performer clause
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) gives the performers their own word-slot before {{ar:نَاسِكُوهُ}} ({{tr:nāsikūhu}}). The clause moves from the singular collective {{ar:أُمَّةٍ}} ({{tr:ummatin}}) to plural agents who enact the appointed rite, and the pronoun also starts the contrast with the later second-person markers in {{ar:يُنَٰزِعُنَّكَ}} ({{tr:yunāziʿunnaka}}) and {{ar:إِنَّكَ}} ({{tr:innaka}}).

topics.headline: detached pronoun foregrounds performers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the community members are explicit performers, not just implied recipients of a rite.
topics.reason: The independent pronoun functions as the subject of the nominal performer clause.

topics.headline: third-person community contrasts with second-person address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah separating ritual communities from the singular addressee who will be contested and then assured.
topics.reason: The pronoun refers back to community members and contrasts with the later second-person object and subject suffixes.

words.gloss_range: active-participle predicate with object suffix: they are performers of that appointed rite
words.root_gloss_range: ritual performance and devotion; local suffix back to the rite selects enacted performance over passive observation
words.prose: {{ar:نَاسِكُوهُ}} ({{tr:nāsikūhu}}) closes the first beat by making the communities performers of the appointed rite. Its plural active participle agrees with {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}), while the final suffix points back to {{ar:مَنسَكًا}} ({{tr:mansakan}}). The result is a closed loop: the rite is assigned for them, and they are characterized by performing it.

topics.headline: active performers of that rite
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rite is not static property; it is the specific practice by which its community is identified.
topics.reason: The active participle predicates performance of the object suffix, whose referent is the appointed ritual noun.

words.gloss_range: resultative conjunction linking universal appointment to prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the first declaration into a consequence. Because every community has an appointed rite, the next clause does not merely sit beside the premise; it follows from it as a prohibition against contention. The boundary from 22:66 is also carried forward: divine giving and human ingratitude become the background for restraining dispute.

topics.headline: appointment premise yields prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ban on contention is inferentially grounded in the universal rite appointment.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the result clause after the opening assignment clause.

topics.headline: 22:66 verdict turns into consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preceding 22:66 verdict becoming a reason why contention over appointed order must be blocked.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect 22:66 to the consequence clause and to the contention over the matter.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negative particle governing the following imperfect verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is not simple description that dispute is absent. In this verbal setting it functions as prohibition, governing {{ar:يُنَٰزِعُنَّكَ}} ({{tr:yunāziʿunnaka}}) and making the clause a restraint on action. Its visible joining after {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) compresses consequence and prohibition into one transition.

topics.headline: prohibitive negation governs the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah issues a ban on disputing, not a neutral report that no dispute occurs.
topics.reason: The following imperfect verb after the negative particle selects the prohibitive reading and blocks nominal genus-negation readings.

words.gloss_range: Form III imperfect under prohibition, with energetic nūn and second-person object suffix
words.root_gloss_range: pulling, extracting, inclination, and contention; local Form III selects reciprocal dispute while variants expose the physical pull image
words.prose: {{ar:يُنَٰزِعُنَّكَ}} ({{tr:yunāziʿunnaka}}) is the ayah’s strongest conflict form. Under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), it restrains third-person disputants, while the energetic ending and final second-person suffix make the addressee the pressured target. The root’s pulling and extraction image remains alive behind the Form III contention sense, and the phrase with {{ar:ٱلْأَمْرِ}} ({{tr:al-amri}}) keeps the dispute focused on the command-matter rather than generic argument.

topics.headline: energetic prohibition targets contention
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the contention is forcefully barred and that the addressee is the object being pressed.
topics.reason: The verb follows prohibitive negation and carries heavy emphasis plus a second-person object suffix.

topics.headline: contention heard against pulling and extraction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices dispute as a pulling contest over orientation, not only as verbal disagreement.
topics.reason: The root family and variant readings expose pulling and extraction, while the canonical Form III keeps reciprocal contention as the selected local sense.

topics.headline: dispute is over the command-matter field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the conflict is about the identified command-matter and separates them from the singular addressed you.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence rows and local prepositional complement connect contention with the following command-matter phrase.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the domain within which contention occurs
words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) governs {{ar:ٱلْأَمْرِ}} ({{tr:al-amri}}) and makes the matter the domain inside which contention happens. Its topical containment sense is selected over temporal location, and the phrase closes the prohibition before the positive command begins.

topics.headline: within the command-matter, not temporal location
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the dispute as contained within a defined issue-field, not as a loose quarrel or a time phrase.
topics.reason: The governed abstract noun selects topical containment, while the prepositional phrase completes the dispute clause.

words.gloss_range: definite abstract command-matter governed as the dispute domain
words.root_gloss_range: command, affair, directive, authority, and ordered matter; local definiteness compresses the known issue into one authority field
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَمْرِ}} ({{tr:al-amri}}) is definite and governed by {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}), so it names the recognizable field in which contention is being blocked. The root range lets matter and command remain together: the dispute concerns an affair, but an affair loaded with directive authority. The word closes the negative beat before the ayah turns to the command to call.

topics.headline: definite matter as dispute domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that contention is not open-ended; it is located in a definite command-matter already made identifiable by the rite appointment.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and genitive after the domain preposition, not the direct object of the dispute verb.

topics.headline: matter carries command-authority pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disputed matter is also an authority field tied to divine command and lordship.
topics.reason: The root family and co-occurrence rows support hierarchy and divine-discourse pressure, while the local abstract noun keeps the field rather than a human commander in view.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction opening a fresh imperative after the completed prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) turns the ayah from restraint to mission. It coordinates the next verbal command with the prohibition but also gives the new directive its own start, so {{ar:ٱدْعُ}} ({{tr:udʿu}}) is not swallowed into the dispute phrase.

topics.headline: from prohibition to positive command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah pairing blocked contention with a constructive command to call.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces a new imperative clause after the prepositional dispute phrase has closed.

words.gloss_range: second-person imperative of calling, with omitted object and direction supplied by the following goal phrase
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, praying, and claiming; local goal preposition selects directed invitation toward the Lord
words.prose: {{ar:ٱدْعُ}} ({{tr:udʿu}}) supplies the positive command after the prohibition. Its object is left unnamed, so the direction phrase carries the focus: the addressee is to call toward {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}), not merely invoke the Lord as the direct object. The clipped imperative form makes the command direct, and the root’s claim-and-call range adds allegiance pressure without replacing the local invitation sense.

topics.headline: call toward, not direct invocation as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command redirects action from disputation toward inviting others to the Lord.
topics.reason: The following goal preposition selects calling toward the Lord and foregrounds direction over an expressed object.

topics.headline: shortened imperative with allegiance shade
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command as immediate and allegiance-oriented, not a neutral speech act.
topics.reason: The weak-final imperative form gives the command its shortened surface, while root-family claim senses remain secondary to the local directed invitation.

words.gloss_range: goal preposition governing the destination of the call
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) turns calling into orientation. It governs {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}), making the Lord the destination toward which the invitation moves rather than the direct object of prayer. As a separate word, it preserves the goal phrase before the assurance clause begins.

topics.headline: goal phrase defines the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mission is defined by direction toward the Lord, not by argument with disputants.
topics.reason: The preposition attaches to the imperative and governs the following Lord noun as the goal of the call.

words.gloss_range: personal Lord noun governed as the goal of the call, definite by second-person suffix
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, nurture, sustaining ownership, mastery, and cultivation; local suffix personalizes the destination of the mission
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:rabbika}}) completes the direction phrase. The second-person suffix makes the goal definite and personal: the call is toward your Lord, not toward an abstract authority label. The root field adds sustaining and cultivating lordship, and the same addressee who was targeted by contention is now bound to the destination of the call. Its link with calling and guidance makes this direction phrase a bridge into the closing assurance.

topics.headline: your Lord as governed call-goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the destination of the mission as personally bound to the addressed messenger.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the goal preposition and definite through the second-person suffix.

topics.headline: lordship includes sustaining care
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the goal of calling as sustaining lordship that links the command to the closing assurance of guidance.
topics.reason: The root family supports nurture, ownership, and mastery; local syntax keeps it as the governed goal of the call.

words.gloss_range: emphatic particle with second-person suffix opening the final assurance clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّكَ}} ({{tr:innaka}}) changes the speech mode from command to confirmed assurance. The attached second-person pronoun becomes the subject of the whole closing predicate, so the addressee moves from being the target of dispute to being the assured subject established upon guidance.

topics.headline: confirmed assurance governs the close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final guidance phrase is not an added description but a confirmed grounding for the command.
topics.reason: The particle governs the second-person subject and opens the emphatic nominal clause whose predicate is the guidance phrase.

topics.headline: same addressee becomes assured subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second-person marker shifting from contested object to caller and finally to assured subject.
topics.reason: The rows track the repeated second-person marker across object, possessive, and subject roles.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām attached to the predicate side of the final assurance
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) adds a second layer of confirmation after {{ar:إِنَّكَ}} ({{tr:innaka}}). Because it attaches to the predicate side and fuses with {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), the emphasis falls on being upon guidance, not on adding new lexical content.

topics.headline: slid lām intensifies the guidance predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final assurance as doubly confirmed, with emphasis placed on the support relation itself.
topics.reason: The lām appears on the predicate side after the emphatic particle and prefixes the support preposition.

words.gloss_range: preposition of support/elevation governing guidance in the final predicate
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) makes guidance the ground beneath the addressee. The closure does not simply say that he has guidance; it pictures him as established upon it. Other senses such as opposition or obligation are narrowed away by {{ar:هُدًى}} ({{tr:hudan}}), leaving the support image to carry the assurance.

topics.headline: guidance as standing-ground
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance as a stable ground on which the addressee stands, not merely as information possessed.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the guidance noun in the predicate; that complement selects the support metaphor and blocks burden or opposition readings.

words.gloss_range: indefinite verbal noun of guidance governed by the support preposition and qualified by uprightness
words.root_gloss_range: guidance, leading, gift, and sacrificial offering; local predicate selects guidance while ritual context preserves led-offering resonance
words.prose: {{ar:هُدًى}} ({{tr:hudan}}) is governed by {{ar:عَلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) and qualified by {{ar:مُّسْتَقِيمٍ}} ({{tr:mustaqīmin}}), so the assurance is being upon a straight kind of guidance. Its verbal-noun form makes guidance itself the support, not a guide-agent. In this ritual ayah, the root’s leading, gift, and led-to-sanctuary offering range adds concrete resonance, while the closing phrase also answers the straight-path wording at 22:54.

topics.headline: guidance governed and qualified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance itself as the support beneath the addressee and as the noun qualified by straightness.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by the support preposition and is modified by the following adjective.

topics.headline: guidance resonates with led offering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance in this ritual context carries a led-to-sanctuary and gift undertone without ceasing to mean guidance.
topics.reason: The root family supports guidance, leading, gift, and sacrificial offering; local predicate grammar selects guidance while preserving ritual resonance.

topics.headline: guidance phrase answers 22:54
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing phrase as a compact guidance-uprightness pairing that resonates with the straight-path wording at 22:54.
topics.reason: The rows identify the local pairing with the following uprightness adjective and give the concrete 22:54 same-surah link.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive active participle agreeing with guidance and closing the ayah
words.root_gloss_range: standing, uprightness, support, peoplehood, and resurrection; local Form X active participle selects maintained uprightness
words.prose: {{ar:مُّسْتَقِيمٍ}} ({{tr:mustaqīmin}}) agrees with {{ar:هُدًى}} ({{tr:hudan}}) and gives the ayah its final word. The adjective keeps the guidance qualitative rather than a fixed title, and the Form X active participle presents uprightness as achieved and maintained rather than passively straightened. The broad root field reaches into standing, support, peoplehood, and resurrection, but the local form narrows that field to straight, stable guidance; the final position makes assurance, not contention, the last weight. It also continues the guidance-uprightness thread visible at 22:54.

topics.headline: indefinite adjective locks to guidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word as the quality of guidance itself, not as a free-floating descriptor.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with the guidance noun in case, gender, number, and indefiniteness and closes the ayah.

topics.headline: Form X uprightness within broad standing field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices straight guidance as standing and self-maintaining orientation, not a passive straightened object.
topics.reason: The root field is broad, but the selected Form X active participle narrows it to achieved and maintained uprightness.

topics.headline: uprightness completes the 22:54 guidance thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final adjective as the established companion of guidance and as part of the 22:54 straight-path thread.
topics.reason: The rows identify the strong guidance-uprightness collocation, a same-surah recurrence, and the community-field bridge.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكًا ... وَادْعُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ... هُدًى مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
baseline_models.mechanism: Exhaustive communal plurality is paired with an appointed, repeatedly enacted rite, while invitation to one Lord and straight guidance provide a common bearing. The forms can differ without making their Lordward orientation plural.

activation_trace.role: Encompassing totality makes the allocation cover every community rather than a favored exception.
A group gathered by a common feature supplies the distinct communal units receiving rites.
Community as a followed way lets the people and their practiced pattern remain semantically intertwined.
Causing something to occupy a condition frames the rite as an assigned ordering, not an accidental custom.
The place and work of devotion give mansak both a concrete setting and an enacted procedure.
Persistence on a way makes the noun-agent repetition describe a community inhabiting its practice.
Calling that inclines through speech supplies a noncoercive motion toward the Lord.
Gentle indication toward road and truth gives the diverse practices a shared directional criterion.
Straightness, balance, and evenness characterize the bearing on which the addressee stands.

changed_reading.before: Each community simply possesses a different ritual.
changed_reading.after: The ayah coordinates exhaustive plurality of enacted communal forms with one Lordward direction; difference of mansak need not equal difference of ultimate bearing.

baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated N-S-K root can specify an appointed sacrificial offering and also the place or performance in which it occurs. The community is therefore not merely assigned a belief but cast as the active performer of a material rite.

activation_trace.role: Appointment into a condition makes the sacrificial procedure an instituted communal form.
The قربان animal and poured blood supply the concrete sacrificial possibility of mansak.
Place and performance keep sacrifice from shrinking to the victim alone; it is a situated rite.

changed_reading.before: Mansak is an unspecified style of worship.
changed_reading.after: Mansak can be heard concretely as an appointed sacrificial performance whose community repeatedly enacts it in a designated ritual setting.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مَنسَكًا هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ ... رَبِّكَ ... هُدًى مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
baseline_models.mechanism: N-S-K carries washing, purification of an ingot, and persistence on a way. Joined to the Lord's nurturing completion and an even course, the community-specific mansak can function as a repeated technology of formation: practice removes admixture and trains a stable direction.

activation_trace.role: Washing and purification supply the cleansing operation latent in ritual performance.
A silver ingot cleared of dross gives the practice a material image of refinement.
Continued use of a way turns purification from a moment into a formative habit.
Repair, nurture, and completion assign the Lord the formative endpoint of the practice.
Course, manner, and intended direction convert refinement into a traversable orientation.
Evenness and rectitude name the stable condition produced by the repeated practice.

changed_reading.before: The rite marks communal identity externally.
changed_reading.after: The rite may also be a community-specific refinery: repeated embodied practice cleans, forms, and stabilizes its practitioners on a Lordward course.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَلَا يُنَازِعُنَّكَ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَادْعُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ
baseline_models.mechanism: Mutual pulling makes dispute a struggle to seize the addressee's position. Because amr can be affair, binding command, authority, or deliberated policy, several disputes coexist: over the rite itself, over who commands it, and over who controls the frame of deliberation. The answering motion is invitation rather than counter-pulling.

activation_trace.role: Reciprocal tugging gives controversy a two-sided struggle for control rather than mere verbal difference.
Affair or condition preserves the broad reading that the contested object is the ritual matter.
Authority and its holder activate a jurisdictional reading of what the parties are pulling over.
Consultation and management of opinion activate competition over the terms of deliberation.
Speech that calls and inclines replaces reciprocal seizure with an open directional appeal.
Lordship and sovereignty identify the authority to whom the disputed matter is redirected.

changed_reading.before: The prophet is told only to win or avoid an argument about ritual law.
changed_reading.after: He is told not to be pulled into a contest for ownership of the affair, command, or forum; his distinct action is to keep directing speech toward the Lord.

context_deltas.mechanism: The near-verbatim formula in 22:34 explicitly places mansak over provision from livestock and the naming of God; 22:36 identifies dedicated animal bodies, while 22:37 denies that flesh is the thing that reaches God and closes with guidance. This strongly concretizes sacrifice while relocating its efficacy from material transfer to God-conscious orientation.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch anchors mansak in a قربان animal and poured blood.
The repeated mansak formula activates the sacrificial branch beside livestock provision and naming God.
Divine uniqueness makes varied communal sacrificial forms converge in the worship of one God.
The dedicated offering animal supplies the concrete body used in the rite.
Literal flesh marks the material component that the verse explicitly denies as the rite's divine endpoint.
Gentle direction to road and truth supplies the nonmaterial telos named after the sacrificial correction.

structural_cues: 22:34 repeats 'for every community We appointed a mansak' before explaining remembrance over provided livestock.
22:36 moves from appointed ritual to dedicated bodies, naming, falling sides, eating, and feeding.
22:37 contrasts flesh and blood with taqwa, then links magnification to prior guidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated formula and the livestock-body-flesh-guidance sequence; I infer that 22:34 glosses the focus mansak and that 22:37 makes ethical orientation, not material delivery, its endpoint. A live alternative is that sacrifice is one salient instance without exhausting the broader place, practice, and habitual-way senses of mansak.

changed_reading.before: Sacrifice is only one dictionary possibility among many for mansak.
changed_reading.after: The surah strongly activates an actual communal sacrifice, yet defines its success through naming, sharing, taqwa, and guidance rather than flesh or blood reaching God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The house sequence orders purification, circumambulation, public summons, travel through open mountain passes, completion of obligations, and renewed circumambulation. That sequence activates mansak as a situated itinerary whose coherent orientation includes both straight travel and circular movement.

activation_trace.role: The focus branch of ritual place and work anchors the itinerary in mansak itself.
Straightness and evenness provide the stable orientation against which the route's varied motions are read.
Removal of impurity prepares the house as the itinerary's usable ritual center.
Rotation around a thing supplies a directed circular action within the rite.
Intentional travel toward what is magnified gives the dispersed travelers one destination.
Wide passes between mountains materialize the converging approach routes.
Completion and finishing mark the itinerary as an ordered sequence with closure.
Established antiquity gives the house temporal depth as the route's enduring center.

structural_cues: 22:26-29 forms a procedural chain from preparing the house to movement, arrival, benefits, sacrifice, completion, and return around the house.
22:27 combines linear arrival from every deep pass with 22:26 and 22:29's circular movement around one center.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an ordered set of places and actions around the house; I infer that this sequence operationally expands the focus sense of 'place and work of ritual' and that straight guidance denotes coherent bearing rather than geometrically straight motion. The live alternative is that the focus mansak is narrower, especially sacrificial, while the itinerary is only its surrounding frame.

changed_reading.before: Mansak is a single ritual slot or isolated act.
changed_reading.after: Mansak can organize a whole pilgrimage itinerary: approach, preparation, circling, sacrifice, completion, and return all hold together under one stable orientation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence in 22:52-54 moves from intrusive casting, through removal and firming, to hearts becoming low and settled, and finally to a straight path. It turns the focus contrast between reciprocal pulling and straight guidance into a dynamic stabilization process rather than a static claim of correctness.

activation_trace.role: Mutual pulling anchors the focus danger as destabilizing contest.
Casting something down supplies the intrusive insertion that disturbs proclamation.
Removal followed by replacement supplies the corrective clearing of the intrusion.
Making firm, exact, and secure supplies the stabilization after removal.
A low, tranquil expanse gives believing hearts a settled receptive posture.
The dying down of fire supplies a coexisting image of agitation subsiding in the heart.
Gentle indication toward the road names the positive motion after interference is cleared.
Rectitude and balance name the path's stabilized condition.

structural_cues: 22:52 orders casting, removal, and firming rather than presenting revelation as untouched by attempted interference.
22:53-54 contrasts diseased or hardened hearts with knowing, believing, humbled hearts before repeating straight-path language.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the interference-correction-settlement-guidance sequence; I infer that the focus prohibition on being pulled into dispute protects the same kind of directional stability and that invitation continues after noise is cleared. A live alternative is that 22:52-54 concerns revelation generally and should not be made a direct explanation of ritual controversy.

changed_reading.before: Being upon straight guidance is a static credential asserted against opponents.
changed_reading.after: Straight guidance is also a recoverable stability: intrusive material is removed, what is true is made firm, hearts settle, and the call can retain its direction despite contest.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate continuation distinguishes opponents' argument from the addressee's required response: answer with God's knowledge, then leave divergent paths to God's judgment at the resurrection. The prohibition therefore limits capture by reciprocal controversy; it does not claim that disagreement will cease.

activation_trace.role: Two-sided pulling supplies the mode of controversy from which the addressee is kept.
Authority and sovereignty make the destination of final adjudication a live issue in the focus.
Twisted, entangled disputation names the opponents' continuing argumentative action.
Judgment between people transfers final settlement away from the present contestants.
Resurrection supplies the deferred temporal forum for final judgment.
Each taking a path unlike the other's preserves real divergence until that judgment.

structural_cues: 22:68 begins conditionally with continued argument and gives a restrained knowledge formula as the reply.
22:69 places judgment over their differences on the day of resurrection.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an immediate sequence from 'do not let them pull you' to 'if they argue' and then divine judgment; I infer that the first command governs the prophet's participation, not the opponents' ability to speak. A live alternative is that the prohibition also authorizes firm present rebuttal, but the supplied reply still withholds final adjudication.

changed_reading.before: The command demands suppression or immediate resolution of ritual disagreement.
changed_reading.after: The command establishes procedural restraint: continue the Lordward invitation, answer argument without entering its tug-of-war, and defer final settlement of persistent divergence to God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing commands spread devotion across bowing, prostration, worship, strenuous exertion, inherited way, regular prayer, and holding fast, while explicitly denying constriction in religion. This strengthens the habitual N-S-K reading: mansak is not only an event but an embodied communal discipline that forms continuity without being defined by oppressive narrowness.

activation_trace.role: Persistence on a way anchors the focus rite as a repeated communal discipline.
Bending and lowering the head supply one recurrent bodily articulation of the way.
Lowering oneself in submission deepens the discipline's embodied humility.
Worship as submissive obedience expands the rite beyond one isolated gesture.
Expenditure of capacity under difficulty supplies sustained effort within the communal way.
Obedience and yielding name the wider religious field in which ritual practice operates.
Narrowness and constriction identify what the appointed discipline explicitly is not meant to impose.
A followed religious way connects the present discipline to Abrahamic inheritance.
A road made recognizable by repeated travel materially reinforces inherited habitual continuity.
A preserving hold supplies cohesion and protection at the discipline's close.

structural_cues: 22:77 stacks bodily worship commands with doing good rather than isolating one ceremony.
22:78 joins effort, divine choosing, absence of constriction, Abrahamic inheritance, communal naming, witness, prayer, almsgiving, and holding fast.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a closing network of repeated bodily and communal practices plus inherited way and non-constriction; I infer that it displays what sustained communal nasak can do across a life. A live alternative is to reserve mansak for the sacrificial or pilgrimage rite and treat the closing discipline as its ethical aftermath rather than its semantic expansion.

changed_reading.before: Mansak is a bounded ceremony that distinguishes one community from another.
changed_reading.after: Mansak can participate in a wider embodied discipline: repeated submission, effort, inherited continuity, social obligation, and protective attachment form a people without making religion a constricted enclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The counterfactual in 22:40 makes divine repulsion of people by one another the condition preventing destruction of several differently named worship habitats, all joined by abundant naming of God. This activates an institutional reading of 'for every community a mansak': differentiated ritual habitats can coexist within a protected ecology rather than compete for erasure.

activation_trace.role: Communities as gathered groups anchor the focus plurality in social bodies.
Ritual place and work anchor the proposed link from community practice to worship habitat.
Turning away harm supplies the protective mechanism that keeps the plural sites from destruction.
The specifically Christian worship-site branch makes institutional difference concrete rather than generic.
Places and houses of prayer supply another distinct worship habitat in the protected list.
The second mapped inventory independently retains prayer places, preserving the split-root evidence.
A place of prostration adds the mosque as a differentiated ritual setting.
Remembrance running on the tongue supplies the common act linking the diverse sites.

structural_cues: 22:40 names multiple kinds of worship site in one destruction counterfactual.
The list closes by describing abundant mention of God's name within them rather than by erasing their distinct names.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine protection, a plural institutional list, and a shared remembrance function; I infer that this is a social habitat in which the focus allocation of communal rites can coexist without mutual erasure. A live alternative is that 22:40 concerns historical protection of worship generally and does not itself authorize every community-specific rite.

changed_reading.before: Different communal rites are merely rival claims to be ranked in argument.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the surah also permits a protected ecology of differentiated worship forms and sites, joined by remembrance of God and bounded against destructive rivalry.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates form-distant H-D-Y branches of gift and sanctuary offering beneath the ordinary focus noun 'guidance.' It remains anchored in the explicit N-S-K sacrificial branch and the focus H-D-Y inventory, but downstream prose must present it only as a semantic echo, never as a replacement translation of huda.

activation_trace.role: The قربان sacrifice supplies the material offering pole of the echo.
A gently dispatched gift to one held in affection lets guidance resonate as something graciously sent.
The offering sent to the sanctuary creates a form-distant return echo between sacrificial mansak and huda.

changed_reading.before: Guidance is only abstract instruction appended after a material rite.
changed_reading.after: As a contained semantic resonance, divine guidance can sound like the gracious counter-gift that redirects sacrificial offering from material transfer toward a Lordward relation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The reading is surprising because it makes the repeated posture 'upon' spatial and load-bearing rather than merely propositional. It remains anchored in the focus phrase 'upon straight guidance' and in 22:11's edge, settling, and face-overturning sequence, but it should be qualified as a structural analogy rather than a claim that the two verses are lexical glosses of one another.

activation_trace.role: A course with direction supplies the surface on which the addressee's stance is imagined.
Balance, evenness, and rectitude make that stance stable rather than marginal.
Inclination away from a direction activates the precarious edge-position contrasted with straight bearing.
Settling and tranquility provide the temporary stability that testing exposes as conditional.
Turning a thing over on its face materializes collapse when an edge-based stance loses support.

changed_reading.before: 'Upon straight guidance' only certifies that the addressee holds a correct proposition.
changed_reading.after: The phrase can also depict a tested, load-bearing stance: unlike worship from an edge that overturns under trial, straight guidance supports continued invitation under argumentative pull.

strongest_changes: The repeated 22:34 formula and 22:36-37 sequence strongly concretize mansak as sacrifice while relocating efficacy from flesh and blood to remembrance, sharing, taqwa, and guidance.
The pilgrimage sequence activates mansak as an ordered place-and-action itinerary in which straight orientation can include circular movement around a stable center.
The immediate 22:68-69 continuation changes the dispute command into procedural restraint and deferred divine adjudication, not suppression of disagreement.
The closing discipline and 22:40's protected worship sites preserve broader habitual and plural-institutional readings alongside the concrete sacrificial one.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah sits at a convergence: an earlier near-duplicate supplies sacrificial content, an interference-to-guidance sequence makes straightness dynamic, and the immediate sequel assigns unresolved difference to divine judgment. The branch inventory also keeps purification, habitual formation, gift, and sanctuary-offering echoes alive without forcing them into one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether focus mansak should be restricted by 22:34 to sacrifice or allowed to retain the broader place, itinerary, and habitual-way senses.
Whether al-amr primarily names the ritual affair, divine command, jurisdiction, or the management of deliberation; the focus grammar supports coexistence more readily than selection.
How much interpretive weight to give the form-distant H-D-Y gift and sanctuary-offering branches beneath the ordinary reading of huda as guidance.
Whether the protected plurality of worship sites in 22:40 directly informs 'every community a mansak' or remains a looser social analogy.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Distinct ritual practice need not become mutual pulling.** `ء م م B004/B005` is community and followed way; repeated `ن س ك B001/B003` worship and rite; `ن ز ع B006/B001` mutual contention as pulling something from place; `ء م ر B001` the affair. Ritual assignments are affirmed before contention is prohibited. I infer that disagreement becomes destructive when one community tries to dislodge the divinely assigned practice or mission of another. The verse preserves ritual plurality while refusing dispossessive dispute.
2. **Invitation replaces tugging with oriented approach.** `د ع و B001` calls to draw near; `ر ب ب B002` nurtures to completion; `ه د ي B002` course; `ق و م B008/B004` straightness maintained. The imperative to call follows the prohibition of mutual pulling. I infer that the proper response to contest is an open directional invitation, not counter-coercion. Guidance reads as a stable platform from which to summon.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:78's “no constriction” and protective holdfast completed the correction: religious exertion is real, but its maintained route is not mutual dispossession.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Assigned ritual plurality is separated from contention over authority.** Fixed `أُمَّة` activates `ء م م:B004` (community), doubled `مَنسَك/نَاسِكُوه` activates `ن س ك:B003` (rite) and `B001` (devotion), and `جَعَلْنَا` uses `ج ع ل:B002` (turning something into an assigned state). The prohibition activates `ن ز ع:B006` (mutual pulling or contention) over `ء م ر:B001` (the affair), while the counter-movement is `د ع و:B001` toward `ر ب ب:B001/B002` (authority and nurturing completion), on `ه د ي:B001` and `ق و م:B008` (straightness). `22:68-70` defer dispute to knowledge, judgment, and record. The packet supplies legitimate differentiated rites and illegitimate pulling over command; I infer that uniformity is not required for straight orientation. The ayah protects plurality while bounding jurisdictional conflict.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: `22:68-70` provide the procedure implicit in the prohibition: answer briefly, relocate evaluation to known work, defer judgment, and trust the encompassing record. This guards plurality without abandoning truth claims.

baseline.text: Her topluluk için uyguladıkları bir ibadet biçimi belirledik. Bu konuda seninle asla çekişmesinler. Rabbine çağır; çünkü sen dosdoğru bir yol üzerindesin.

findings.text: Her topluluğa ayrı ibadet yolu verilmesi, ritüel çeşitliliğini Rabbin otoritesi hakkındaki çekişmeden ayırır.
Çağrı, karşılıklı çekiştirmenin yerine insanı Rabbine doğru yönelten bir yaklaşma yolu koyar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı, keskinlik veya iş görme gücünün azalmasıyla insanın, hayvanın, rüzgarın ve duyuların yorulmasını aynı çekirdekte toplar. Verilen dal bu ortak güçten düşme sınırını doğru biçimde yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal bütünlük bildiren kullanımları ve mirasla ilgili akrabalık anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın güçten düşme anlamını kapsar; bineği yorma anlamı ise yalnız belirtilen ettirgen söz öbeğine bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın, hayvanın, aracın, organın ya da etkin gücün keskinliğini, dayanma gücünü veya iş görme yetisini yitirerek körelmesi ya da yorulmasıdır. Bineği bu duruma düşürme, ayrıca belirli bir ettirgen söz öbeğinde anlatılır.

facets.statement: Keskinliğin, gücün veya iş görme yetisinin azalması temel anlamdır.
Yürüyen insanın ya da hayvanın yorulması ve kılıç, dil, bakış, işitme veya rüzgarın etkisizleşmesi bu çekirdeğin gerçekleşmeleridir.
Belirli ettirgen söz öbeği, kişinin bineğini yorup güçten düşürmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yorulma ile keskinliğini veya etkinliğini yitirmeyi ortak bir güçten düşme alanında birleştirir; kullanım insan, hayvan, kılıç, dil, bakış, işitme ve rüzgar gibi farklı taşıyıcılara uzanır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Keskinlik, dayanma gücü veya etkinlik kaybının birlikte anlatıldığı dal çekirdeğine uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Hem körelmeyi hem de yorularak güçten düşmeyi korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsan veya hayvanın yürüme ve çalışma sonucu güçten düştüğü bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Canlı taşıyıcının yorulma ve güç kaybını eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kılıç, dil, bakış veya başka bir etkin yetinin keskinliğini yitirdiği bağlamlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Keskinlik ve etkinlik kaybını doğal bir Türkçe karşılıkla korur.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal bedensel yorgunlukla sınırlıyken bu dal, aynı güç kaybını araçların keskinliği ile dilin ve duyuların etkinliğine de taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, başkasının bakımına ve geçimine yük olan kişiyi çekirdek yapar; yetim, yakın desteği bulunmayan kişi ve bakmakla yükümlü olunan kimse bu alanda sayılır. Dal kullanılabilir, ancak bütün bu kişileri özleri gereği değersizleştiren bir niteleme gibi okunmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Buradaki ağırlık fiziksel ağırlık değil, bir başkasının üstlendiği bakım ve geçim yüküdür.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın ad bağımlı kişiyi veya yükü bildirir; akrabaların kişiye yük olması gibi okumalar yalnız verilen söz öbeklerine bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bakımı, geçimi veya taşınması başkasının sorumluluğuna yük olan kişi ya da şeydir. Yetim, çocuğu bulunmayan kişi veya hem çocuğu hem de ebeveyni bulunmayan kişi gibi geleneksel adlandırmalar ile akrabaların birine bağımlı hale gelmesi bu çekirdeğe bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi ya da şeyin bakım, geçim veya taşıma bakımından başkasına yük olması çekirdektir.
Yetim, çocuğu bulunmayan kişi veya hem çocuğu hem ebeveyni bulunmayan kişi kanıta bağlı özel referanslardır.
Taşınan tapınma nesnesi ve geçimi bir kişiye kalan akrabalar, bağımlılık ilişkisinin söz öbeğine bağlı örnekleridir.
Kaynak anlatımında ağır tabiatlı kişi ve başkası adına iş gören kişi de bu adlandırmanın çevresinde anılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek, geçimi veya bakımı bir başkasının üzerinde kalan bağımlı kişi ya da şeydir. Yetim, çocuğu bulunmayan kişi ve hem çocuğu hem ebeveyni bulunmayan kişi öne çıkan özel durumlar, taşınan nesne ile geçimi üstlenilen akrabalar ise ilişkiyi somutlaştıran kullanımlardır. Bir kaynak, ağır tabiatlı kişiyi ve başkası adına iş gören kişiyi de bu adlandırma çevresinde anar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Geçim, bakım veya taşıma sorumluluğunun başka bir kişiye düştüğü çekirdek ilişkiye uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Bağımlı olan tarafı ve yükü üstlenen başka tarafı birlikte korur.

error_profile.preserves: Bakım sorumluluğunu ve bağımlı kişiler topluluğunu açıkça korur.
